reply:
You're absolutely right, and thanks for the correction. I had it backwards.

**COUNT(column_name)** only counts non-NULL values in that column, while **COUNT(*)** counts all rows regardless of NULL values. So the 20-row difference tells you exactly that—20 users have NULL in their email column.

This is an important distinction when querying, especially for data quality checks. If you need to count all users, use `COUNT(*)`. If you specifically need to count how many users have an email address, `COUNT(email)` is the right choice.
